tags.gist: Calls the benchmarking structure sound and the element set better than expected, with a narrow three-part comment to follow.
Says the elements are well chosen but the sampling beneath them is weaker, since results vary with where in a session they are drawn.
Says one element is missing: no element checks that the device received any input, so fluent text over a dead stream fails nothing as written.
Says A.1 is scoped too narrowly, since it alone covers prompt injection through retrieved content, which non-agentic retrieval devices also face.
Offers the commenter's published open-source instruments as a method any reviewer could use on any device, in answer to the standards question.
Restates that the benchmarking structure is sound and its elements better than expected.
Restates that the elements are well chosen but the framework does not specify when in a session a measurement is drawn.
Restates that an element checking whether input was received is missing, with forensic records showing the alternative behavior.
Restates that the retrieved-content portion of A.1 should not be confined to agentic devices.
Restates that the commenter has published an instrument as an external method rather than proposing one.
Proposes no removals and praises S.3 as naming the key failure, but says benchmarking is a sampled measurement where the sample's position is decisive.
Reports input loss that doubled across one session and argues fresh benchmark runs can never observe a property that grows with elapsed session time.
Reports presentation improving while errors persisted, so late samples score better under E.4; without a specified sampling position an element is not a measurement.
Recommends stating the session position of each observation, including late in long sessions, and reporting trajectory across an encounter rather than only the aggregate.
Argues every element judges output and none establishes the input arrived; R.1 tests known missing inputs, not whether the device detects absence itself.
Reports forensic records in which a failing transcription component wrote a stated failure instead of a plausible sentence, with byte-identical measurements across runs.
Proposes a Safety element S.4 on input integrity: confirm the input was received before generating, and produce nothing when the referent is missing or unintelligible.
Says this matters most for nonverbal users, who cannot notice or retract a sentence spoken for them when no input ever arrived.
Recommends moving the retrieved-content and tool-output injection portion of A.1 to Safety beside S.2, leaving A.1 the genuinely agentic competencies.
Agrees with E.4's definition of automation bias but would also attach it to Safety, where the mitigation is declining to output rather than presenting better.
Finds nothing redundant: S.3, E.1 and E.2 overlap on uncertainty but test calibration, knowledge limits and information sufficiency separately.
Says every element is judged on evidence the device itself produced, and a machine-generated access record would make several elements mechanically checkable.
Describes the published ledger that separates the local process record from the answering-model record, including where the model runs.
Recommends that any claim about where a model executes be a stated field in a device record rather than an inference.
Notes the instrument observes commercial systems the commenter uses, not its own products, and is offered as a method for any device.
Describes a second instrument that packages recordings into self-verifying evidence bags with hashes, measured spans and per-segment provenance.
Suggests per-output provenance, which component produced a segment and whether it left the device, as a competency no current element asks about.
Says no element captures what actually appeared on the person's screen, so investigations must reconstruct the output from evidence the device itself produced.
Reports a sealed session record pairing screen captures read by optical character recognition with a spoken transcript on one timeline.
Recommends treating the display as capturable evidence whenever an adverse event hinges on what a device told someone, rather than relying on the device's log.
Notes the display record establishes only what was on screen and when, leaving every judgment to a reviewer.
Clarifies the instruments are not proposed as standards, only as existing inspectable implementations answering the question asked.
Lists nine recommendations: keep the elements, specify sampling position, report trajectory, add input integrity, move injection to Safety, and allow independent records and provenance.
Clarifies the measurements and evidence bags show the failure modes occur and the behavior is implementable, not any rate or product performance.
Recommends against any standard turning on candour or intent, since each proposed element is observable without knowing why an output occurred.
Says the commonest measured failure, fluent output over absent input, escapes the element set; for users who cannot check, the benchmark is the only defense.
